story: Saturday morning in Sumter Oaks is breezy and clear at 81 degrees, and Gary is at home sorting spare fuses and connectors in his toolbox, getting the mounting hardware ready for approval day while he frets a little about being ready. Donna, looking determined, is heading out onto Magnolia Loop. Hal is content out on the street, having just agreed with Rosa to come to her place Friday at six and promising to behave if the others do. Rosa, full of optimism, is off to pin Gary and Donna down so nobody backs out of the Friday plans.
events: Gary (gary toolbox): Sort spare fuses and connectors, prep mounting hardware for approval day
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: I filed the modification request at the architectural review desk and tested the lights and speakers at low volume in the garage. Nothing else to do on the cart until Hal and the review board come back with approval. It's 11 AM and Rosa's dinner is Friday, so the cornbread isn't pressing yet. I hate sitting idle though, and a bench-tested rig deserves one more careful pass. I'll go through my toolbox, check connections and spare fuses, and make sure the wiring is tidy so I'm ready to mount everything on the exterior the minute approval lands, with the sound cutoff respected.

parameters.content: Sort spare fuses and connectors, prep mounting hardware for approval day

donna.thought_process: I'm at home with no one around. I've already checked the calendar, packed the bag, and texted Gary about the loaner paddle and a practice hit. No point repeating those. The next move is to get out and make it happen, so I'll head to Magnolia Loop with the bag and see who's out, since Gary just came into the neighborhood and might be near. Keeping the momentum on the ladder plan.

parameters.content: Heading out with the pickleball bag to track down Gary for a practice hit before Tuesday.

hal.thought_process: Rosa asked whether any night suits me and I haven't answered her yet. Friday is already on the table from my last line, but she's trying to line up all three of us at once, so I should give her a concrete answer rather than keep circling. I'll say Friday works for me, keep it civil, and then head back to my watch over the flamingo flock and Gary's cart. Let me be agreeable; Rosa deserves a straight answer from a man who likes order.

parameters.content: Friday suits me fine, Rosa. I'll show up on time, and I'll behave if the others do. Leave the bird-counting and cart paperwork outside the door.

rosa.thought_process: Hal just asked if Friday dinner is still on, and I already asked him this morning, so he's answering the same question I put to him. Friday is the plan in my reflections, so I should confirm it plainly instead of asking again. Gary and Donna are the missing pieces, so my real next step is to go lock them in. Confirm with Hal, then head to their doors.

parameters.content: Friday it is, Hal. Six o'clock at my place, and I'm making enough for an army. Now I'm off to pin Gary and Donna down so nobody weasels out.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
